title: Domain Events
description: Learn to model and use domain events effectively in event-driven microservices.

data.text: Domain events are events that represent something significant that happened in the domain. Amazon, Netflix, and Uber model their systems around domain events like OrderPlaced, PaymentSucceeded, and ShipmentDelivered. Well-designed domain events are the foundation of event-driven microservices.

Good domain events are named in past tense (OrderCreated, not CreateOrder), contain all data consumers need, and are immutable. They represent facts that have already occurred, not intentions to do something.

data.title: Event Design Rules
items: Name in past tense: OrderCreated, not CreateOrder
Immutable: Never modify or delete published events
Self-contained: Include all data consumers need
Time-stamped: Include when the event occurred
Idempotent: Include an event ID for deduplication

data.title: Event Naming Convention
data.text: Use the pattern <Entity><Action>: OrderCreated, PaymentProcessed, UserRegistered. This makes events immediately understandable and consistent across the organization.

items.question: What is the difference between domain events and integration events?
items.answer: Domain events represent something that happened in the domain. Integration events are published for external systems. In practice, they are often the same event used for both internal and external communication.

items.question: How do I handle event versioning?
items.answer: Add a version field to the event schema. When you change an event, increment the version. Consumers should handle both old and new versions during migration.

items.question: Should events contain IDs or full objects?
items.answer: Include enough data for consumers to act. Often this means IDs plus key fields. Avoid embedding large objects; let consumers fetch details via API if needed.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Domain events represent facts that happened in the domain
Use past tense naming: OrderCreated, not CreateOrder
Events should be immutable and self-contained
Good event design reduces coupling and improves maintainability
data.takeaway: Well-designed domain events are the foundation of maintainable event-driven microservices.
